children: Pre-owned goods marketplace Circle has raised Rs 25 crore in a seed funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from Titan Capital and Myntra co-founder Raveen Sastry. Ajith Pai, chief operating officer of Delhivery, has also joined the round as an angel investor.
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand beyond Bengaluru, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and expand its network of Trust Hubs and logistics infrastructure.

Founded by Chirag Kataruka and his co-founder, Circle focuses on consumer-to-consumer (C2C) commerce, enabling individuals to buy and sell pre-owned goods. The platform combines AI-based technology, human verification and managed fulfilment to facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers.

The funding comes a little over a year after Circle went live, according to a LinkedIn announcement by the company’s co-founder. The company aims to make transactions involving pre-owned goods more accessible and reliable for consumers.
